Frank

/frank/ — rhymes with bank · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is frank is open, honest, and direct.

Her frank feedback surprised the team, but everyone appreciated the honesty.

Worked Example

A young designer asks her mentor what he really thinks of her portfolio. Instead of softening his answer with compliments, he tells her plainly which three pieces are weak and exactly why, holding nothing back.

His honesty is open and direct, delivered without hedging or sugarcoating — that plainspoken quality is what frank means. Frank is more precise than 'honest' because an honest person may still soften or withhold, while a frank one says it straight out.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

candid: Candid means honest in an open, unguarded way -- the truth as it spills out, like a candid photo catching someone unposed. Frank is more deliberate: a frank speaker chooses to state a hard truth plainly. Candid honesty slips out; frank honesty is set down on purpose.

direct: Direct describes the route a statement takes: straight to the point, without detours or evasion, whatever the topic. Frank is about content as well as route -- openly stating truths that others might soften. You can be direct about which bus to take; you are frank about bad news.

forthright: Forthright means volunteering your honest view before anyone asks for it, plainly and without hesitation. Frank concerns the openness of what is said, asked-for or not: hard truths stated without softening. A forthright person speaks up first; a frank person speaks plainly whenever they speak.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

evasive: avoiding clear and direct answers

guarded: careful not to reveal true thoughts

Where it sits · how little the truth gets softened — tactful → honest → frank → blunt

tactful vs. frank: Tactful is weaker than frank in directness — a tactful speaker cushions the truth to spare feelings, while a frank speaker states it openly.

honest vs. frank: Honest is weaker than frank; an honest person tells the truth when asked, but a frank person volunteers the plain truth even when it's uncomfortable.

blunt vs. frank: Blunt is stronger than frank — frank feedback is open and honest, while blunt feedback is so direct it may feel harsh.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — frank

root — frank: free; free-spoken (Old French (franc), from Late Latin francus 'free')

Put it together

Put it together: From Old French franc, 'free': in early medieval France only the fully free could speak openly, so frank came to mean free-spoken — open, honest, and direct.

Use the root in a new word: franchise

Use the root in a new word: franchise: The fast-food franchise opened its hundredth restaurant this year.

Word Building

Word Choice

Frank describes speech that is direct and unreserved, sometimes bluntly so (to be frank with you...), and carries a slightly more deliberate, formal feel than a casual synonym like 'blunt.'
